_note: Filled from a real annotated passage in creator-reference-4-full.json (unit VU_081, 631.0-645.0s). Used as a worked example because the project's own 30 annotated passages were not readable at design time. The narration text is the analysis cue, not a verbatim transcript, so it is marked as such.

scriptRef.sectionPurpose: Establish a documented pattern of aggressive legal retaliation.

narration.text: Trumps responded by countersuing the Department of Justice for a hundred million
narration.precedingText: The Justice Department filed suit over the rental practices.

takeaway: Trump counter-sued the government for an enormous sum, and the court threw it out.

claims.text: The Trumps countersued the Department of Justice for $100 million.
sourceCandidates: the filed countersuit document, page showing the damages figure
court record or contemporaneous reporting showing the dismissal

requiredMedia.contentRequirement: The countersuit filing itself, cropped to the passage naming the Department of Justice and the $100 million figure, with the dismissal language reachable in the same document or a second page.

legibilityRequirement.smallestMeaningfulElement: the damages figure and the dismissal clause

visualEvents.triggerPhrase: countersue the Justice Department for 100 million
visualEvents.description: Highlight travels to the countersuit clause and the damages figure becomes legible.
Highlight moves to the dismissal clause.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not imply the countersuit succeeded or was partially upheld.
prohibitions.reason: The narration says it was dismissed outright.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not show a stock or generic legal document, gavel, or courthouse.
prohibitions.reason: The obligation is exact_source_required; a representative stand-in would present decoration as proof.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not show modern courtroom footage.

successConditions: The viewer can read the $100 million figure while it is spoken.
The viewer can read the dismissal while it is spoken.
The document is identifiable as the actual filing.
failureConditions: The document text is too small or on screen too briefly to read.
A generic legal document stands in for the actual filing.
The highlight lands before or after the phrase it belongs to.
The dismissal is never shown, leaving the countersuit looking successful.

openQuestions: Is the actual filing obtainable, or only contemporaneous reporting about it?
